About Capco

Capco is a global technology and business consultancy, focused on the financial services sector. We are passionate about helping our clients succeed in an ever-changing industry.

We're looking for a senior software engineer with strong ML and GenAI skills to deliver end-to-end machine learning solutions for our financial services clients. You'll own the full lifecycle — from data pipelines and model development through production deployment and monitoring — working autonomously in complex, regulated environments.

This is your chance to make a real difference!

  • Design and build end-to-end data pipelines and feature engineering workflows on large-scale transactional data in regulated client environments
  • Train, calibrate, and validate ML models — supervised, unsupervised, and ensemble — including threshold analysis and production-grade explainability
  • Develop GenAI-powered solutions such as agentic workflows, RAG systems, and LLM-based automation to accelerate knowledge-intensive client processes

  • Practical GenAI experience: LLM integration, prompt engineering, RAG architectures, and agentic workflows for automating knowledge-intensive processes
  • Fluent German and strong client-facing communication skills, with the ability to produce audit-ready documentation for regulated environments

 

Ready to take the Next Step 

If this sounds like you, we would love to hear from you.  This is an opportunity to make a difference and contribute to a highly successful company with a significant growth trajectory.

The startup team of the AWS Frontier AI Services puts applied scientists to work directly with those founders and their engineers. We're hiring a Senior Applied Scientist in North America to own those engagements with our strategists end to end: scope the problem with the founding team, design and run the experiments, and ship working code into the startup's stack on AWS. The problems are open-ended and the timelines run in weeks, so your scientific judgment sets both the approach and the bar for done. Then deliver against them in six-to-twelve-week engagements, with the startup's own engineers working alongside you. - Improve model quality for the startup's use case by post-training open-weight models. Profile where the compute goes, apply quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, batching, parallelism and kernel-level tuning, and measure cost per output before and after. - Invent new methods when published ones fall short of the customer's target, and publish the results at peer-reviewed venues, on AWS blogs and as open-source code. - Turn each engagement into assets the next one can reuse: reference implementations, evaluation harnesses and playbooks. Take the gaps you find in Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker and AWS Trainium back to those service teams as specific requests. - Raise the science bar on the team. After lunch you join an AWS account manager and a GenAI strategist to scope a request from a voice AI company that needs lower inference latency before it scales up.
